atoms.name: Latches and flip-flops
atoms.one_line: A latch is level-sensitive and transparent while enabled; a flip-flop samples on a clock edge; a NAND SR latch holds at $\bar S=\bar R=1$.

atoms.name: Characteristic equations
atoms.one_line: $D:\ Q^+=D$. $T:\ Q^+=T\oplus Q$. $JK:\ Q^+=J\bar Q+\bar KQ$. $SR:\ Q^+=S+\bar RQ$ with $SR=0$.

atoms.name: Flip-flop conversion
atoms.one_line: $J=K=T$ gives T; $J=D,K=\bar D$ gives D; $D=\bar Q$ gives a divide-by-2 toggle stage.

atoms.name: Ripple counters
atoms.one_line: Each stage is clocked by the previous output; frequency drops by 2 per stage and settling time grows with $n$.

atoms.name: Synchronous counter design
atoms.one_line: Write the next-state table, convert with the excitation table, minimise each flip-flop input.

atoms.name: Modulus, ring and Johnson counters
atoms.one_line: Mod-$N$ needs $\lceil\log_2N\rceil$ flip-flops; ring has $n$ states, Johnson has $2n$.

atoms.name: State sequences of circuits
atoms.one_line: Write the next-state equations, update every flip-flop from the old state, step until the state repeats.

atoms.name: FSM states and Mealy outputs
atoms.one_line: Minimise by partition refinement; a Mealy output depends on state and input, a Moore output on state only.
